explain.say: Imagine you walk towards a wall, and each step covers half the gap that is left. You get closer and closer. Do you ever touch it? This curve, 1 minus 1 over x, does the same. Look at the yellow mark: when x is 1, the value is 0.

explain.say: Let us zoom in on the gap to 1. At x equals 100 the gap is 0.01. At 1000 it is just 0.001. See it shrink? That is a limit: a value you can get as close to as you like.

explain.say: So the limit is 1, the last mark, even though the curve never lands on it. Well done! This one idea, as close as you like, is the seed of all of calculus. Speed at an instant and the area under a curve are both built on it.

faq.q: What is a limit in maths?
faq.a: A limit is the value a function gets closer and closer to as x moves towards a number or grows without end. You can get as close as you like, even if you never land on it.

faq.q: Does the curve ever reach the limit?
faq.a: Not always. 1 minus 1 over x never equals 1 for any real x, but it gets as close as you want. Some functions do reach their limit, and that is fine too.
asks: Can a function equal its limit?

faq.a: Limits let us talk about speed at one instant or the exact area under a curve, where plain arithmetic would make us divide by zero. Calculus is built on them.
lim is short for limit. You read lim as x tends to infinity of f of x as: the value f of x settles towards when x grows without end.
asks: How do you read limit notation?

faq.a: Yes. If the values keep jumping between two numbers, or grow without end, there is no single number to approach, so the limit does not exist.
asks: When does a limit not exist?

facts: The limit of 1 − 1/x as x tends to infinity is 1.
The precise epsilon-delta definition of a limit was developed in the 1800s by Augustin-Louis Cauchy and Karl Weierstrass.

quiz.why: 1 over x shrinks towards 0, so 1 minus it gets as close to 1 as you like.

wrong.0: 0 is the value at x = 1, where the curve starts, not where it settles.
wrong.2: The values settle towards one number, 1, so the limit exists.
